To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the adult thymus is a dynamic and highly plastic tissue which, under certain circumstances, may be able to undergo substantial alterations in its size and cellularity.
the thymus of intact and orchidectomised rats of different age are characterized by different thymopoietic patterns.

the thymopoiesic alterations in the peripubertal orchidectomised rats of different age were characterized by a transient enlargement and enrichment of the lymphoid cellularity, and that the age-associated alterations of the thymopoietic process were reflected by the reshaping of the thymocyte differentiation pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a possible involvement of gonadal hormones in shaping the thymus structure, size and intrathyic T cell matration in the course of the life span.
a putative role for male gonadal hormones (testosterone and its metabolites, e.g. estradiol) in the regulation of thymopoiesic processes.
the elucidation of the mechanisms of the age-related changes in thymopoietic processes, and their modulation by male gonadal hormones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thymic size and cellularity are not only under the control of gonadal hormones but are also subjected to the influence of the age-related alterations in the hormonal status of the intact animals.

the thymus of intact and orchidectomised adult rats is not a stable organ, but rather a dynamic system which is subjected to significant changes in the thymus cellularity, size and intrathmic T cell maturation, depending on the age and hormonal milieu of the host.

the thymic alterations observed in adult rats following the peripubertal gonadectomy are not a result of the gonadal hormones deficiency per se, but rather of the age-related changes in the gonadal hormone levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in adult rats, the thymus is capable to maintain the thymocyte production and to provide a proper T cell maturation in the presence of the low level of circulating gonadal hormones.
in adult rats the gonadal steroid hormones are involved in the regulation of thymopoiesic processes, which are subjected to age-related changes.
the gonadal hormones, especially testosterone, play an important role in shaping the T cell differentiation in the thymus.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the thymus of the rat is capable of sustaining the thymic T cell production for a prolonged period of time, but the quality of this production is not stable, and may be subjected to significant changes.

, although the thymus in adult rats is capable to sustain the production of new T cells, the age-associated decline in the thymus function is not a consequence of the diminishing of the thymopoiesic activity, but rather is due to an age-dependent impairment in the thymic ability to provide efficient maturation of the thymocytes.
the gonadal hormones play a role in the regulation of thymopoiesic processes in adult rats, and that the effects of the gonadal hormone deprivation are age-dependent.
